cards.explanation: The answer is to confront her with all her abominations, friends. God tells Ezekiel, the prophet He's speaking to, to confront the city of bloodshed with all her abominations (Ezekiel 22:2). It's not a job anybody puts on a vision board. I think I'd have asked if there was a smaller assignment, like sweeping the bakery.

The answer is idols, friends. God says the city brings her own doom by shedding blood within her walls and making idols to defile herself (Ezekiel 22:3). Two things are named, and the blood comes first. Verse 4 says she's guilty of the blood and defiled by the idols she made.

The answer is that they will mock her, friends. God says it plainly: “Those near and far will mock you, O infamous city, full of turmoil.” (Ezekiel 22:5) Verse 4 says He has made her a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the lands. Near and far both get a say. I know a little about being the punchline myself.
The answer is False, friends. God says, “Father and mother are treated with contempt.” (Ezekiel 22:7) Contempt, not honor. It's one line in a long list of what's happening inside her walls.

The answer is the fatherless and the widow, friends. God says, “…the foreign resident is exploited, the fatherless and the widow are oppressed.” (Ezekiel 22:7) Three groups are named in that one verse. I think this one hits hard, and it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is profaned, friends. God says, “You have despised My holy things and profaned My Sabbaths.” (Ezekiel 22:8) Holy things got treated like common ones. Two charges in one sentence, and they go together.

The answer is forgotten, friends. After the bribes and the extortion, God says, “But Me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD.” (Ezekiel 22:12) The city is the one who forgot, not God. I know a thing or two about being left in the back of a drawer, and this one hits me too.
The answer is True, friends. God says, “I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will act.” (Ezekiel 22:14) He's not hinting and He's not guessing. When He says it, He means it.

The answer is that He will scatter them among the nations, friends. God says, “I will disperse you among the nations and scatter you throughout the lands; I will purge your uncleanness.” (Ezekiel 22:15) Dispersed and scattered, and both words are there. It's a heavy word, so I'll just let it sit.

The answer is that she will know He is the LORD, friends. God says that when she has defiled herself in the eyes of the nations, she will know that He is the LORD (Ezekiel 22:16). It's a phrase that shows up again in this chapter, in verse 22. She forgot Him, and she'll know Him.

The answer is Jerusalem, friends. God says, “Because all of you have become dross, behold, I will gather you into Jerusalem.” (Ezekiel 22:19) The furnace picture comes next. Dross is the leftover scum that gets skimmed off when metal is melted.

The answer is True, friends. God says, “…I will gather you in My anger and wrath, leave you there, and melt you.” (Ezekiel 22:20) The furnace picture is clear, with the gathering first and the melting after. It's a heavy word, and I won't make it lighter than it is.

The answer is cleansed, friends. God says, “In the day of indignation, you are a land that has not been cleansed, upon which no rain has fallen.” (Ezekiel 22:24) That's the word that fills the blank. He's speaking about the day of indignation.

The answer is the widows, friends. God says the princes “…devour the people, seize the treasures and precious things, and multiply the widows within her.” (Ezekiel 22:25) That's a sober line. I think it's one to hold quietly.

The answer is common, friends. God says the priests “…make no distinction between the holy and the common, and they fail to distinguish between the clean and the unclean.” (Ezekiel 22:26) The people who should know the difference don't draw the line. They also disregard His Sabbaths.

The answer is that they whitewash them with false visions, friends. God says, “Her prophets whitewash these deeds by false visions and lying divinations…” (Ezekiel 22:28). It's like painting over a crack in the wall and calling the house fine. The crack is still there.

The answer is False, friends. God says, “The people of the land have practiced extortion and committed robbery. They have oppressed the poor and needy and have exploited the foreign resident without justice.” (Ezekiel 22:29) It isn't only the leaders. The whole land is in this.

The answer is no one, friends. God says, “I searched for a man among them to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, so that I should not destroy it. But I found no one.” (Ezekiel 22:30) I think this is the heaviest line in the chapter. It deserves a quiet moment.
